correctness.rationale: C PASS: For any non-ultimately-periodic one-sided binary word u, its XOR derivative d cannot be ultimately h-periodic because that forces u_(i+2h)=u_i eventually. Every E-antipalindromic factor projects to a palindromic derivative factor with at most two binary lifts; C_d(n-1)<=C_u(n). Shallit Theorem 4 on d yields P_E(n)log(P_E(n)+1)/C_u(n)->0; Shallit also makes ordinary reversal palindromes negligible for u. With H-language invariance, complement fixes no word and Burnside forces C_H(n)/C_u(n)->1/4 without assumed convergence. Odd n and empty factors do not affect asymptotics.
